t: An imperial city from 1218, Zürich was ruled by guilds after Rudolf Brun’s revolution of 1336 and joined the Confederacy in 1351.
Its citizens governed a large rural territory through bailiffs, and the city led the Confederacy as its Vorort.
Under Zwingli and Bullinger it became a fountainhead of Reformed Protestantism with influence across Europe.
dyk: The Zürich Bible, printed by Christoph Froschauer, was completed in 1531, three years before Martin Luther’s complete German Bible appeared.
ev: The Zähringen line dies out and Zürich becomes an imperial city
Rudolf Brun overthrows the old council and introduces guild rule
Zürich joins the Old Swiss Confederacy
Zürich is defeated at St. Jakob an der Sihl in the Old Zürich War
Burgomaster Hans Waldmann is overthrown and executed
Huldrych Zwingli begins preaching at the Grossmünster
Zwingli is killed at the Battle of Kappel
The French invasion ends the old regime; Zürich joins the Helvetic Republic

f.successor: Helvetic Republic; from 1803 the Canton of Zürich
